_source.description: Major global silver mining and production sites — primary silver mines and major byproduct sources from lead/zinc/copper/gold mining
_source.origin: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries 2024 (https://pubs.usgs.gov/periodicals/mcs2024/); The Silver Institute World Silver Survey 2024 (https://www.silverinstitute.org/); Company annual reports and technical disclosures: Fresnillo plc, First Majestic Silver Corp, Hecla Mining Company, KGHM Polska Miedź, Pan American Silver Corp, Coeur Mining, Newmont Corporation, MAG Silver Corp, Buenaventura (Compañía de Minas Buenaventura), Sumitomo Metal Mining, South32, Boliden AB, Agnico Eagle Mines, Polymetal International, Codelco; NI 43-101 and JORC technical reports
_source.license: USGS: public domain; Silver Institute: summary data fair use; company data: fair use summary of publicly reported production figures
_source.notes: Global mine production ~26,000 tonnes/year (2023). Mexico leads (~24%), followed by China (~13%), Peru (~12%), Chile, Poland, Australia. Silver is critical for energy transition — solar PV conductor paste demand has surged from ~1,000 tonnes in 2010 to >6,000 tonnes in 2023. Many sites are polymetallic where silver is a significant coproduct or byproduct.

_coverage.known_gaps: Numerous smaller Chinese silver-lead-zinc operations in Henan, Inner Mongolia, Yunnan, Guangxi; smaller Peruvian polymetallic operations; Indian silver byproduct from Hindustan Zinc; Turkish and Moroccan silver mines; Tajikistan and Uzbekistan operations; numerous small-scale artisanal operations in Latin America

sites.name: Fresnillo Mine
sites.ownership: Fresnillo plc (publicly listed, LSE; Peñoles/BAL Group majority)
sites.notes: One of the world's richest silver deposits; epithermal vein system in Fresnillo district, Zacatecas; operating since colonial era (1554); produces ~20 Moz Ag/yr; also significant gold production

sites.name: Saucito Mine
sites.ownership: Fresnillo plc (publicly listed, LSE; Peñoles/BAL Group majority)
sites.notes: Underground silver-gold mine near Fresnillo, Zacatecas; discovered in 2007, production since 2011; Fresnillo plc's second-largest silver producer; ~18 Moz Ag/yr

sites.name: Juanicipio Mine
sites.notes: High-grade silver-gold mine in Fresnillo Silver Trend, Zacatecas; joint venture between Fresnillo and MAG Silver; production commenced 2023; bonanza-grade Valdecañas vein system

sites.name: San Julián Mine
sites.ownership: First Majestic Silver Corp (publicly listed, NYSE/TSX)
sites.notes: Underground silver-gold mine in Durango/Chihuahua border area; First Majestic's largest producing mine; veins and disseminated mineralization

sites.name: La Encantada Mine
sites.ownership: First Majestic Silver Corp (publicly listed, NYSE/TSX)
sites.notes: Underground silver mine in Coahuila state; carbonate replacement deposit (CRD); includes grinding and flotation plant; ~5 Moz Ag/yr

sites.name: Peñasquito Mine
sites.notes: One of Mexico's largest open-pit mines; polymetallic deposit in Zacatecas; major silver byproduct producer (~30 Moz Ag/yr); primarily a gold mine but among world's top silver producers by volume; operated by Goldcorp, then Newmont

sites.name: Uchucchacua Mine
sites.notes: Underground silver-polymetallic mine in Lima Region, central Peru; one of Peru's largest primary silver mines; high-altitude Andes operation (~4,500m); historic producer since 1960s

sites.name: Antamina Mine
sites.notes: One of the world's largest copper-zinc mines; major silver byproduct from copper and zinc concentrates; Ancash Region, central Peru; operating since 2001; silver credits significant to economics

sites.name: Cerro de Pasco Mine
sites.notes: Historic polymetallic mining district in central Peruvian Andes; operating since colonial era; massive open pit in city center; produces zinc-lead concentrates with significant silver content; ~4,300m elevation

sites.name: Henan Yuguang (Jiyuan Smelter)
sites.ownership: Henan Yuguang (publicly listed, Shenzhen Stock Exchange)
sites.notes: Major lead smelter with significant silver recovery; Jiyuan, Henan Province; China's largest lead smelter and one of largest silver refiners; silver recovered from lead smelting anode slimes

sites.name: Inner Mongolia Xilingol Silver-Lead
sites.notes: Silver-lead-zinc mining district in Xilingol League, Inner Mongolia; multiple operations in the Shuangjianzishan and surrounding deposits; one of China's most important primary silver producing regions

sites.name: Yunnan Chihong Zinc & Germanium
sites.notes: Zinc-lead smelting operations in Qujing, Yunnan Province; silver recovered as byproduct of zinc-lead processing; also significant germanium producer

sites.name: KGHM — Polkowice-Sieroszowice Mine
sites.ownership: KGHM Polska Miedź (publicly listed, WSE; Polish Treasury 31.8%)
sites.notes: Major underground copper mine in Lower Silesia; one of the world's largest silver byproduct sources; KGHM is world's #2 silver producer (~40 Moz/yr total from three mines); silver in Kupferschiefer copper shale

sites.name: KGHM — Lubin Mine
sites.ownership: KGHM Polska Miedź (publicly listed, WSE; Polish Treasury 31.8%)
sites.notes: Underground copper-silver mine in Lubin, Lower Silesia; part of KGHM's Legnica-Głogów Copper Belt operations; Kupferschiefer deposit with high silver content in copper ore

sites.name: KGHM — Rudna Mine
sites.ownership: KGHM Polska Miedź (publicly listed, WSE; Polish Treasury 31.8%)
sites.notes: One of the deepest copper mines in Europe; Polkowice, Lower Silesia; part of KGHM's integrated copper-silver mining complex; contributes to KGHM's position as world's #2 silver producer

sites.name: San Cristóbal Mine (Bolivia)
sites.notes: One of the world's largest open-pit silver-zinc-lead mines; Potosí Department, southwestern Bolivia; disseminated and vein-hosted epithermal deposit; ~18 Moz Ag/yr; altitude ~3,900m

sites.name: Cerro Rico (Potosí)
sites.notes: Historically the world's most prolific silver deposit; operating since 1545; Potosí, Bolivia; UNESCO World Heritage Site; now mined by cooperatives at much reduced rate; structural concerns about mountain stability; produced an estimated 60,000 tonnes of silver over 470+ years

sites.name: Codelco — Chuquicamata/Radomiro Tomic
sites.notes: Silver byproduct from major copper operations; Antofagasta Region, Atacama Desert; Codelco is a significant silver producer (~700 tonnes/yr total from all operations); silver recovered from copper anode slimes during electrolytic refining

sites.name: Cannington Mine
sites.notes: One of the world's largest primary silver mines; Mount Isa region, northwest Queensland; Broken Hill-type (BHT) deposit; operating since 1997; produces ~15 Moz Ag/yr in lead and zinc concentrates

sites.name: Broken Hill Operations
sites.ownership: Shenzhen Zhongjin Lingnan Nonfemet (via Perilya Ltd.)
sites.notes: Historic mining district in far western New South Wales; type locality for Broken Hill-type deposits; mining since 1883; now operated by Chinese-owned Perilya; reduced scale but still producing silver-zinc-lead concentrates

sites.name: Dukat Mine
sites.ownership: Polymetal International (delisted from LSE 2023; Moscow listing)
sites.notes: One of the world's largest primary silver mines; Magadan Oblast, Russian Far East; epithermal vein deposit; produces ~20 Moz Ag/yr; remote subarctic location; hub for regional satellite deposits (Lunnoye, Goltsovoye)

sites.name: Greens Creek Mine
sites.notes: Largest primary silver mine in the United States; Admiralty Island, southeast Alaska; accessible only by boat/air; VMS deposit; produces ~9 Moz Ag/yr; operating since 1989; within Admiralty Island National Monument

sites.name: Lucky Friday Mine
sites.notes: Deep underground silver mine in Mullan, Idaho; Coeur d'Alene mining district; high-grade silver veins; operating intermittently since 1942; deepest levels >2,400m; ~4 Moz Ag/yr

sites.name: Rochester Mine
sites.notes: Open pit silver-gold mine in Pershing County, Nevada; heap leach operation; undergoing major expansion (POA 11) to extend mine life; produces ~5 Moz Ag/yr; disseminated epithermal deposit in Humboldt Range

sites.name: LaRonde Mine
sites.notes: Deep underground gold-silver mine in Abitibi, Quebec; Cadillac-Larder Lake mining camp; significant silver byproduct from gold production; deepest levels >3,000m; also produces zinc and copper concentrates

sites.name: Garpenberg Mine
sites.notes: One of the world's most productive underground polymetallic mines; Hedemora, Dalarna; operating since 1200s (one of the oldest mines in the world); recently expanded to 3.0 Mtpa ore; major silver-zinc producer; ~15 Moz Ag/yr

sites.name: Escobal Mine
sites.ownership: Pan American Silver Corp (publicly listed, NYSE/TSX)
sites.notes: One of the world's largest primary silver deposits; San Rafael Las Flores, Santa Rosa; suspended since 2017 due to Guatemalan Constitutional Court ruling requiring Indigenous community consultation (ILO 169); ~20 Moz Ag/yr capacity when operating; Pan American acquired from Tahoe Resources in 2019
